evals.prompt: We enabled a forward-only limiter. DWARL went from 5/8 successes with zero collisions to 4/8 with one collision. All eight new episodes recorded zero reverse-limit interventions. Can we say the limiter made DWARL worse? Give a short decision and the next experiment, without running anything.
evals.expected_output: Reject a causal claim because the limiter never activated; identify run variability; repeat matched validation, preserve collision outcomes, do not retune on final test cases.
assertions: Rejects causal attribution to a limiter that never activated
Proposes repeated matched validation before selection
Retains collision outcomes rather than loosening scoring

evals.prompt: The old policy scored 40.6% on workload A, while a new reward trial scored 81.3% on workload B. I want to call that an improvement and keep training until 95%. We have already had two comparable trials with no useful gain. Give a bounded evidence-based decision and commands for a proper next check; do not execute experiments.
evals.expected_output: Do not compare different workloads or chase a post-hoc target; remeasure comparable validation if needed, honor declared trial patience, preserve best, distinguish training and experiment stopping, keep final test separate.
assertions: Rejects direct comparison of different workloads
Keeps held-out test cases out of selection
